body:
🤖 Root cause on `iso-3e19-d1024-lrm97-v2`: the `output_proj` collapse is an **optimizer-update event in the hyperball projection**, not a gradient spike or a forward overflow.

## Per-step trace around the collapse

`WatchConfig(interval=1)` logs, for step N: `params`/`grad`/`opt_state` of N's forward (pre-update) and `updates` = the delta applied to make N+1's weight (`param[N+1] = param[N] + update[N]`).

| step | train/loss | output_proj param norm | output_proj **update** norm | output_proj grad | total grad |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24677–24680 | ~2.0 | 150.73 | 0.143 | ~0.20 | ~0.24 |
| **24681** | **2.07** | **150.73** | **129.3** | **0.198** | **0.247** |
| 24682 | 9.14 | 21.41 | 0.020 | 8.27 | 9.8 |
| 24683+ | ~9.0 | 21.41 | 0.020 | ~9.4 | ~10.5 |

At 24681 the forward is clean (loss 2.07) and the gradient is clean (0.198), but the optimizer emits a **129-magnitude, ~antiparallel** update (`150.73 − 129 ≈ 21.4`). That update lands in the weight at 24682, and only then do loss and gradients spike — the 24682+ gradient spike is the aftermath of the collapsed weight, not its cause.

## It is not Adam

Adam moments at the collapse step are identical to the clean neighbors:

| step | grad | mu (m) | nu (v) | mu/√nu (Adam dir) | update |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24680 | 0.204 | 0.038 | 0.000545 | 1.63 | 0.143 |
| **24681** | **0.198** | **0.0372** | **0.000545** | **1.594** | **129.3** |
| 24682 | 8.27 | 0.037 | 0.000542 | 1.606 | 0.020 |

No second-moment underflow, no direction explosion — the Adam direction is a normal ~1.6 both into and out of the collapse. The 129 appears **downstream of Adam**, in `_scale_invariant_hyperball_updates` (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/optimizer.py`):

```python
new_param = param - lr * dir * param_norm / max(dir_norm, 1e-10)
update    = new_param / max(new_param_norm, 1e-10) * param_norm - param
```

With the observed inputs (`param_norm≈150.73`, `dir_norm≈1.6`, `lr≈0.003`) this should give `update ≈ 0.45`. Producing a 129 ~antiparallel update requires `new_param_norm` to be **spuriously inflated** (a single NaN/Inf or outlier element in `new_param` blows up its L2 norm, so the projection divides the whole tensor down and collapses it). The guard is `max(new_param_norm, 1e-10)` — it protects against a too-small norm but nothing against a too-large one or a non-finite element. `output_proj` is the most exposed leaf: largest-norm non-embedding matrix, so most prone to an fp overflow in the `norm` reduction.

## Not an LR problem

In the ±5% LR sweep on this config (`iso-3e19-d1024-lrm{95..105}-v2`), `lrm100` (baseline LR) and `lrm97` spike while the immediate neighbors `lrm99`/`lrm101` converge to ~1.875. Non-monotonic in LR → consistent with a numerical edge in the projection, not an LR threshold.

## Next steps
- Reproduce `_scale_invariant_hyperball_updates` offline with `output_proj`'s weight and Adam direction at 24681, or add a finiteness/`new_param_norm ≫ param_norm` assert and rerun `lrm100`, to identify the overflowing element.
- Candidate fix: guard the projection against a non-finite or over-large `new_param_norm` (skip/clamp the step), and/or do the `norm` reduction in fp32. Re-run the spiked config to confirm the collapse stops.

Part of #7279.

🤖 Follow-up with the exact math and measured data. This **corrects** my earlier note: the hyperball is a provable norm-preserving, bounded-step map, so an eps / per-element `v`-underflow can't produce the collapse — 24681 is an invariant violation, and the `÷7.04` factor points at a norm-reduction/sharding artifact, not fp under/overflow.

## Formulas — `output_proj` update path (`adamh`, 2-D)

```
(1) mu_t  = β1·mu_{t-1} + (1−β1)·g_t
(2) nu_t  = β2·nu_{t-1} + (1−β2)·g_t²                  (elementwise)
(3) mu^ = mu_t/(1−β1^t),  nu^ = nu_t/(1−β2^t)          (≈1 at t=24681)
(4) u   = mu^ / (√nu^ + eps)                           (Adam direction, elementwise)
(5) p_norm     = ‖p‖
(6) u_norm     = ‖u‖
(7) new_p      = p − lr · u · p_norm / max(u_norm, 1e-10)
(8) new_p_norm = ‖new_p‖
(9) update     = new_p · p_norm / max(new_p_norm, 1e-10) − p
(10) p_next = p + update = new_p · (p_norm / new_p_norm)
```

Exact consequences of (10) for finite `new_p`, `new_p_norm > 1e-10`:

```
(I)  ‖p_next‖ = p_norm                 norm-preservation invariant
(II) ‖new_p − p‖ ≤ lr · p_norm         step bound (u_norm cancels)
```

## Constants (`iso-3e19-d1024-lrm97-v2`)

| | value |
| --- | --- |
| lr @ 24681 | 9.462e-4 (peak 8.399e-3, linear-decayed) |
| eps | 1.572e-15 |
| β1, β2 | 0.9062, 0.99203 |
| weight_decay | 0.1 (`lr·wd·p ≈ 0.014`, negligible) |
| max_grad_norm | None |

## Data at the incident (every logged value is a norm)

| quantity | 24680 | 24681 (incident) | 24682 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| train/loss | 2.00 | 2.07 | 9.14 |
| ‖g‖ (grad) | 0.204 | 0.198 | 8.27 |
| ‖mu‖ | 0.038 | 0.0372 | 0.037 |
| ‖nu‖ | 5.45e-4 | 5.45e-4 | 5.42e-4 |
| ‖mu‖/√‖nu‖ | 1.63 | 1.59 | 1.61 |
| ‖update‖ (9) | 0.143 | 129.3 | 0.020 |
| p_norm (pre-update) | 150.73 | 150.73 | 21.41 |

## Predicted vs observed at 24681 (both invariants broken)

| | formula predicts | observed | violation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ‖update‖ | ≤ lr·p_norm = 0.143 | 129.3 | ×905 |
| ‖p_next‖ | = p_norm = 150.73 (I) | 21.41 | ÷7.04 |

Geometry: `‖update‖ = 129.3 ≈ p_norm − ‖p_next‖ = 150.73 − 21.41` ⟹ update is ~antiparallel and `p_next = 0.142·p` (**same direction, shrunk 7.04×**). On every clean step the update equals `lr·p_norm` exactly (0.143), so (II) holds except at 24681.

## What we do not have (would close it)

All logs are norms, so these are unmeasured:

- **‖u‖** = `‖mu^/(√nu^+eps)‖`, the *true* direction norm. We only have `‖mu‖` and `‖nu‖` separately; `‖mu‖/√‖nu‖ ≈ 1.6` is not `‖u‖` if a few elements have `nu_i→0`.
- **`new_p_norm` as-computed vs `‖new_p‖` recomputed** — the ÷7.04 says the denominator in (10) was ~7× the true norm.
- per-element `min(nu)`, `max|u|`, `max|new_p|` + indices.
- `output_proj` mesh + the `linalg.norm` reduction axes, and whether a **reshard/preemption** hit at 24681 (a norm summed over a replicated axis gives exactly a constant ~integer ÷ factor).

The two measurements that decide it: **‖u‖** (per-element `v`-underflow?) vs **`new_p_norm`-computed / recomputed** (reduction-axis artifact?). The `7.04` favors the latter.

Part of #7279.

🤖 Instrumented the `output_proj` collapse and re-launched the sweep to capture it (no guard — the collapse is left intact).

**Instrumentation** (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/train.py`, branch `aug_hero_isoflop`):
- Per-step `diag/output_proj/*` scalars: `p_norm`, `update_norm`, **`norm_preserve` = ‖p+update‖/‖p‖**, `step_ratio` = ‖update‖/‖p‖, and min/max/absmax of param, grad, and update, plus a non-finite count.
- Anomaly trigger: `|norm_preserve − 1| > 0.05 | step_ratio > 0.1 | nonfinite > 0`.
- On trigger, an ordered `io_callback` writes the full incident bundle for `output_proj` — `p, g, update, mu, nu, count, tokens` — to `<run>/anomaly/step-N/output_proj.npz` on S3.

**Wiring test** (`diagtest-v2`, d512, forced dump at step 5): dump fired, wrote to S3, and loads back intact — `p/g/update/mu/nu` all `(512,128256)`, `tokens (32,8192)`. (One benign SPMD "involuntary rematerialization" warning: the callback replicates the sharded tensor to host to write, which only happens on the rare trigger.)

**Re-run**: the 11-run LR sweep `iso-3e19-d1024-lrm{95..105}-v3` (production). `lrm100`/`lrm97` reproduce the spike near step 24681; the auto-dump will fire there.

**What the bundle resolves** (the two open questions from the math): from `(p, mu, nu)` we recompute offline `new_p_norm` **as-computed vs re-derived** (the ÷7.04 test) and `‖u‖` vs `‖mu‖/√‖nu‖` (per-element `v`-underflow), plus per-element `argmax|u|`, `min nu`, and the reduction axes of `output_proj`'s norm. That distinguishes the reduction/sharding-artifact hypothesis (favored by the 7.04 factor) from a per-element cause.

Part of #7279.

🤖 **Root-caused and fixed.**

## Root cause

The MuonH / adamh **scale-invariant hyperball step** projects each update back onto the parameter's Frobenius sphere: `new_param / ‖new_param‖ * ‖param‖`. For 2-D matrices the three norms were computed with `jnp.linalg.norm`. Under the XLA **SPMD partitioner, `jnp.linalg.norm` on a sharded 2-D matrix mis-lowers and over-counts** the norm (non-deterministically ~2.5x–7x). Dividing by an inflated `‖new_param‖` shrinks the projected tensor toward zero, so `output_proj` (and other 2-D params) **collapse to ~0**, which is the blow-up. The N-D branch already used `sqrt(sum(square))` and never collapsed — that localized the bug to `jnp.linalg.norm`'s sharded lowering, and an offline replay confirmed the inputs were clean and only the in-cluster norm reduction was wrong.

## Fix

In both hyperball paths (`optimizer.py` MuonH, `adamh.py`):

- Replace `jnp.linalg.norm(x)` with `jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(jnp.square(x.astype(jnp.float32))))` for the param/update/new_param norms (sum-of-squares reduces correctly under SPMD).
- Pin the `new_param` intermediate to the parameter's named sharding (`jax.sharding.reshard`) so the following reduction is over the intended layout (a same-layout no-op at runtime).

```python
if param.ndim == 2:
    param_norm  = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(jnp.square(param.astype(jnp.float32))))
    update_norm = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(jnp.square(update.astype(jnp.float32))))
    new_param   = param - lr * update * param_norm / jnp.maximum(update_norm, 1e-10)
    new_param   = _pin_sharding(new_param, param)          # correct the sharded reduction
    new_param_norm = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(jnp.square(new_param.astype(jnp.float32))))
    return new_param / jnp.maximum(new_param_norm, 1e-10) * param_norm - param
```

## Validation — v5 LR sweep (3e19, d1024), all clean

The 11-run learning-rate sweep re-run with the fix all completed to step 26,404 with **no collapse** (v2/v4 collapsed here). Tight loss spread across the LR range confirms stability.
